main_body: Thatched-roof hut: a large thatch roof slope (rows 0-36) over a timber-and-plank wall with a plank door, a shuttered window and a stone step (rows 37-63).
top_band: Light golden thatch roof slope, rows 1-35, ending in a bright eave edge at rows 34-35 with a dark eave line at rows 36-37. Row bands of thatch repeat down the slope.
evidence: The roof is a big foreshortened slope surface that overhangs the wall, like the reference tile roofs. Under the bright eave edge (rows 34-35) a dark shadow row (36-37) separates it from the wall. The wall has its own front face, with a door in a dark frame and a shuttered window set into the planks. Both roof and wall read correctly, with no receding side face, so this is a 3/4 building.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 6 tones with per-row highlights, so the roof shading is decent and 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 0%. But the piece has only 29 distinct colours against 66 and 185 for the references. Its median of 10 colours per tile is below the 18 of h101 and about level with the 11 of h112. 78% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% for the references, so the silhouette has a black sticker-like outline instead of a tinted material-tone one. The wall planks and door are simple repeated stripes with little grain. Overall it is thinner and more sticker-like than the references.
